study.title: 1 Corinthians 1 - Unity in Christ and the glory of the cross
study.overview: In this chapter, Paul presents himself as an apostle called by the will of God, addresses the church of God in Corinth and begins the letter with grace and peace. Then he thanks for the grace already received by the Corinthians and states that God will sustain them to the end. The central problem of the chapter is the inner division of the church, in which different groups identified with human leaders. Paul corrects this spirit of party reminding that Christ is not divided and that the message of the cross should not be emptied by human rhetoric. The chapter ends with the great reversal of the gospel: God saves through what the world calls weakness, so that no one may boast before him, but only in the Lord.

outline.title: Apostolic greeting and church identity
outline.explanation: Paul affirms his apostolic authority as a gift and vocation of God, and calls the Corinthians of God's church, sanctified in Christ and included in the communion of all who call upon the name of Jesus.

outline.title: Thanksgiving, gifts and perseverance
outline.explanation: Paul thanks for the grace given to the Corinthians, the gifts and the testimony confirmed among them, and remembers that God will sustain them to the end for communion with the Son.

outline.title: The appeal to unity and correction of factions
outline.explanation: Paul pleads for agreement and denounces the disputes around human leaders. He insists that his main mission is to evangelize, not to build personal prestige, so that the cross of Christ does not lose his central place.

outline.title: The Cross, God's Wisdom and the End of Human Pride
outline.explanation: The message of the cross divides humanity between those who perish and those who are saved. God frustrates human self-confidence, chooses what the world despises and makes Christ's wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption of the believer, so that all glory belongs to the Lord.

study.context: By the notes of Adam Clarke, Corinth was a well-known city of Greece, important for its position between ports and trade routes. The note also records that the church there was planted by Paul around 52 A.D. This background helps to understand why the church had strong contact with values of status, eloquence and competition, precisely the elements faced by Paul throughout the chapter.
study.theology: The chapter teaches that the church belongs to God, not to its human leaders, and that Christian holiness is born of union with Christ. Grace comes before performance, sustains the believer and preserves it to the end. Paul rejects the logic of religious vanity: the cross is not adornment of discourse, but the center of God's saving power. Therefore, divine wisdom appears paradoxically in what the world calls madness. Salvation then excludes human pride and establishes a standard of Christian life in which all confidence and all glory are displaced to the Lord. In evangelical reading, this highlights the sufficiency of Christ, the effectiveness of preaching the gospel, and the total dependence on grace.

scholarViews.insight: Paul quotes Jeremiah to show that there is no room for human pride, because salvation is the result of God's sovereign power and not of self- merit.
Paul exhorts unity not merely in an administrative tone, but appealing to the name of Christ, to correct the divisions and fleshly comparisons among the brethren.
In calling believers "sanctified in Christ Jesus" and "holy calls," the text indicates separation from the corruptions of the place and the time as part of the purpose of the gospel.

questions: What forms of division or preference for human leaders still try to replace the centrality of Christ in the church today?
Does my way of hearing and evaluating preaching value the cross of Christ or just human eloquence and prestige?
In which areas of my life do I still seek personal glory, instead of boasting only in the Lord?
study.practice: Read this chapter as a practical call to humility: examine whether your opinions, choices and relationships in the church are promoting unity around Christ. Submit your sense of value to the cross, recognizing that all that you are in Christ comes from grace. Also practice a concrete trust in the simple preaching of the gospel: instead of seeking appearance, status or self-confirmation, ask God to make you someone who points to Christ and not to yourself.
study.uncertainty: The notes do not detail all possible historical debates about the exact date of the letter or the identity of each name cited; therefore, I mentioned only what is explicitly supported by the comments provided. I also treated confessional interpretations as readings, not as undeniable facts of the text.
